lesson 01 SQL foundations · beginner

Meet your first SELECT

Choose columns and read rows from a table.

THE IDEA

A table is a set of rows with named columns. SELECT lists the columns you want; FROM names the table that holds them. In Retail, every row of customers is one identified wholesale customer and every row of products is one stock code. A query reads rows; it never changes them. Worked steps sometimes end with LIMIT so you only preview a few rows. LIMIT is not part of the pattern, and nothing grades it until its own lesson.

DATASET: RETAIL

customers
4 columns · 848 rows
products
6 columns · 5,304 rows

COMMON MISTAKE

SELECT * returns every column, including ones the task did not ask for. A checked answer must return exactly the requested columns, in the requested order.

Understand the Retail invoices

Follow one invoice from orders to its lines in order_items and its products. Which columns identify a sale versus a cancellation, and which rows have no customer?

Retail · 5 related tables

TABLES

categories
17 rows · 3 columns
products
5,304 rows · 6 columns
customers
848 rows · 4 columns
orders
6,722 rows · 6 columns
order_items
125,613 rows · 7 columns

RELATIONSHIPS

How to join these tables. Left column matches the right column.

products.category_id → 
joins to
categories.category_id
orders.customer_id → 
joins to
customers.customer_id
order_items.order_id → 
joins to
orders.order_id
order_items.stock_code → 
joins to
products.stock_code
Before you analyze
orders has one row per invoice header; order_type is 'sale' or 'cancellation'. order_items has one row per invoice line and joins to orders on order_id.
Line value is quantity × unit_price: cancellation lines are negative, and a few lines on sale invoices are negative adjustments too. customer_id is NULL on anonymous invoices. products.category_id links to categories, which groups products into departments; some products have no category.
The data ends on 9 December 2011, so December 2011 is incomplete.
